Hi Samantha — great question, thanks for flagging. High-level summary below; I attached a concise RFP-ready writeup and a decision matrix.

Quick pros/cons:
- AWS/Azure/GCP Marketplace (Private Offer)
  - Pros: consolidated billing under your cloud invoice, faster procurement for customers who prefer marketplace POs, opportunity for AWS co-sell if Redwood qualifies and you engage the AWS AM, simplified SaaS onboarding for some SSO/billing workflows.
  - Cons: marketplace commercial terms are often standard (limited ability to negotiate some clauses); there can be revenue share fees and platform-specific entitlement mechanics; custom indemnity or data residency controls may require a private offer or additional paperwork.

- Direct Enterprise Agreement with Redwood
  - Pros: full flexibility on legal terms (SLA, indemnities, data controls), tailored invoicing, and the ability to put detailed support and escalation paths into the contract. Also preferred when you need on-prem/VPC deployment and KMS integrations.
  - Cons: can take longer to finalize (legal review, redlines), and requires Redwood to support your billing process (net terms, PO handling).

Notes on co-sell: if you go through AWS Marketplace private offer and we activate the APN co-sell engagement, there are potential deal registration and co-sell incentives for the AWS seller/partner side. That can help with credits or prioritized support from AWS, but it doesn’t change Redwood’s ability to offer custom contract terms if a private offer is needed.

I attached: ACME-RFP-response.pdf (redacted), Redwood-Marketplace-vs-Direct-Decision-Matrix.xlsx, and a sample Private Offer pack (Redwood-PrivateOffer-AWS.pdf).

If helpful, we can set a quick call with our legal and partnerships lead to talk tradeoffs for the specific clauses you care about (data processing, audit rights, indemnities).

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Looping in procurement/legal notes here. A few practical points for the RFP:

- Invoicing: Marketplace will map to Acme's cloud bill which most procurement teams like for consolidated spend. If Acme needs monthly Redwood invoices and net-60 terms, a direct contract is cleaner.
- Support/SLA: We enforce the same SLAs across both purchase paths for hosted Redwood API; however, enterprise contracts allow specific remedies and credits to be written in.
- Data & Security: For VPC/private deployment, we always prefer EA/direct since Marketplace SaaS can be limited for air-gapped/on-prem constraints.
- Marketplace private offers can be used with custom pricing and some additional T&Cs, but it requires partner ops to set up the private offer and sometimes an MSA addendum.

Suggested RFP wording (short):
"Redwood supports both Marketplace private-offer purchases and direct enterprise agreements. Marketplace provides faster procurement and consolidated cloud invoicing; direct agreements provide maximum contractual latitude for data, indemnity, and SLA customizations. Redwood can support a Marketplace private-offer with customized pricing or a direct enterprise amendment to meet Acme’s legal requirements."

I'll attach a single-slide decision matrix for the sales thread.

- Laura
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Samantha — attaching the RFP-ready language and a one-sheet matrix (see attachments). Quick decision guidance tailored to Acme:

1) If speed is the primary constraint (PO via AWS billing), choose AWS Marketplace Private Offer. Redwood will:
   - Create a private offer tied to Acme’s AWS account
   - Provide the private-offer pricing and entitlement SKU mapping
   - Liaise with AWS Partner team for any co-sell enablement

2) If you require custom indemnities, audit rights, or an on-prem/VPC deployment, opt for a Direct Enterprise Agreement. Timeline: expect 3–6 weeks for legal redlines; we will prioritize the review if you share the RFP clauses now.

Next steps I propose:
- If Marketplace is preferred: confirm Acme AWS account ID and we’ll submit a private offer request to AWS (I can coordinate with our partner manager).
- If Direct EA: send over your RFP clauses and procurement contact; Laura and our counsel will prepare an initial redline.

Would you like me to schedule a 30-minute call with our legal/partner ops to walk through both flows?
